bug: Only one index (i) is returned; the result must contain both indices.
0 is treated as a valid floor, so an all-negative array returns 0 instead of the largest (least negative) element.
The i % 15 branch is unreachable because multiples of 15 are caught by the i % 3 branch first.
Off-by-one between loop and return: for n = 3 it returns 2 instead of 3 (should return curr).
No base case for an empty node (null); root.left is accessed on null, which throws a TypeError.
current.next is overwritten before the original next node is saved, so the traversal loses the rest of the list.
Values are never added to seen, so duplicates can never be detected.
A single stack gives LIFO behaviour; pop returns the newest item where a queue must return the oldest.
The base case returns 1 for n = 0; F(0) must be 0.
The loop stops when left == right without checking that last candidate; nums=[5], target=5 returns -1.
